subject: research/shapley-sampling
professional: a researcher in data valuation and cooperative-game approximation (the Castro 2009 / Maleki 2013 / Mitchell 2022 literature) reviewing for a workshop or main-track ML venue; first checks: do the exact variances and Shapley values recompute by brute force, is cost counted in value-function evaluations (model retrainings) rather than marginals, is stratum allocation and the concentration bound the standard modern choice, and what is new over the published samplers

evidence.correctness: Reran `PYTHONPATH=src python3 experiments/run.py` (21 s) and diffed with experiments/results.txt: identical. Independent brute force in scratchpad/indep.py (does not import the package; enumerates all 8! = 40,320 permutations of the spread game w=[0.05..2.0]): Shapley values match exact_shapley to 6 d.p. ([0.012429 ... 0.28445], sum 0.996482 = v(N)); exact permutation-estimator RMSE at m=96 is 0.01831, size-stratified 0.00754, variance ratio 5.893 (results.txt E1: 0.01831, 0.00754, 5.89); one-whale ratio 8.376 (8.38). Closed forms: equal weights phi_i = v(N)/n = 0.119905 and the n=2 formula (v1+v12-v2)/2 = 0.172728, 0.580675 both match exact_shapley. Hoeffding ln(2n/delta)/(2 eps^2) by hand: 1154, 7211, 28842 (matches). I also computed the antithetic estimator's variance exactly (average of pi and reverse(pi) over all 8! permutations), which the author only simulated: exact RMSE at 48 pairs 0.01117 vs simulated 0.01118, variance ratio 2.69 vs the paper's 2.6. Every reported number is right. One derived claim is off: the '4-5x conservative' Hoeffding looseness is measured on a power-of-two grid; on a step-16 grid with the same seed the empirical need is 176 and 1056 permutations, so looseness is 6.6x and 6.8x (understated, conservative direction, grid disclosed in the paper).
evidence.completeness: Everything the README lists runs: 9 tests pass in 0.86 s ('9 tests, ~1 s'), run.py finishes in 21 s ('under a minute') and reproduces results.txt byte for byte, figure.py run in a scratch copy reproduces rank_recovery.svg byte for byte (cmp). E1-E5 in the whitepaper each have code and output. No TODOs or stubs. Not done and not claimed: joint/shared-strata sampling, n>10, any second game (stated in Limits). Live page not loaded (marisstella.app is proxy-blocked in this session); the homepage summary in research/_homepage/projects.json:498 matches the README numbers.
evidence.verification: `cd research/shapley-sampling && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: 9 OK, 0.859 s. The variance-prediction tests are good (they compare simulation with the exact formula, and caught an 8% inflation of perm_second_moment). Five mutants with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: caught 2 (Shapley weight comb(n-1,k) -> comb(n-1,min(k,1)); perm second moment x1.08); survived 3: sample_perm_antithetic reusing idx instead of its reverse (the 1.6x antithetic headline has no test at all), dropping the factor 2 in Hoeffding's ln(2n/delta) (the test only asserts > 20000), and strat_var using n-1 instead of n in the per-stratum variance (the 15% tolerance absorbs it).
evidence.craft: Read src/shapley_sampling/model.py (117 lines), __init__.py, tests/test_model.py, experiments/run.py, experiments/figure.py. Small, stdlib-only, readable, seeded; figure parses results.txt rather than retyping numbers. Defects: E1's printed header says 'm=100 marginal evals/player' but m = 100 - 100 % n = 96 for the n=8 games (run.py:11 vs :14); sample_perm and sample_perm_antithetic duplicate the telescoping loop and hard-code this game's marginal instead of calling marginal(); sample_perm_antithetic silently uses m-1 permutations for odd m; strat_var/sample_strat give k=0 (a single, zero-variance stratum) the same budget as every other stratum; the samplers are game-specific, so the 'auditing' tool cannot take a user's v.
evidence.claims: Backed: every figure in README.md:3, the whitepaper abstract and the homepage summary (recomputed above), '9 tests ~1 s', 'under a minute', efficiency of permutation and antithetic sampling (exact telescoping, gap 0 in E3), 'exactly zero-variance for equal contributors' (tested, and true for any symmetric game), Limits section honest about one stylised game and n<=10. Not backed or overstated: (1) 'size-stratified sampling has 6-8x lower variance' and 'about 4x fewer samples' for top-3 recovery are at equal *marginal* evaluations (stated only in whitepaper.md:9); each stratified marginal costs two value-function evaluations (two model retrainings in the motivating training-contributor setting) while a permutation yields n marginals for n+1 evaluations, so at equal retraining budget the spread-game ratio is about 3x (3.1), not 5.9x; the README and homepage drop the qualifier. (2) 'Hoeffding sample count is 4-5x more than needed' is 6.6-6.8x on a finer grid. (3) The paper presents (i)-(v) as findings with no citation to Castro et al. 2009 (permutation sampling, efficiency), Maleki et al. 2013 (stratified sampling with Hoeffding bounds), Castro et al. 2017 (stratified with optimal allocation), Illes and Kerenyi 2019 / Mitchell et al. 2022 (antithetic and other correlated permutations); 'Related:' lists only in-repo projects (whitepaper.md:25).
evidence.fitness: Job: a researcher or payer wants to know which sampler to use for Shapley payments to training contributors and how many samples to promise. They get a clean, reproducible toy: exact variance formulas for n<=10 in one closed-form submodular game. They cannot build on it as research: every finding is known (permutation efficiency, Castro 2009; stratification beats plain permutation and Hoeffding sizing, Maleki 2013; antithetic permutations cut variance in monotone/submodular games, Mitchell et al. 2022, which compares antithetic, orthogonal, Sobol and kernel-herding permutations on real models and is the nearest prior work), there is no comparison with KernelSHAP / unbiased KernelSHAP (Covert and Lee 2021) or Neyman-allocated stratification, no real valuation game (data Shapley on an actual model), and cost is counted in marginals rather than retrainings. A payer could not use it either: the samplers hard-code the toy game's marginal. As research it is a textbook exercise, well executed.
evidence.domain: Against current Shapley-approximation practice: (a) cost is measured in value-function calls; here in marginals, which flatters stratification 2x; (b) stratum budgets are allocated by Neyman/variance-proportional allocation (Castro 2017, Maleki 2013), not uniformly, and the k=0 stratum, which has one set and zero variance, gets 1/n of the budget; (c) sample-size guarantees use Bernstein or empirical-Bernstein bounds and the actual marginal range (here at most 0.842, which alone cuts the Hoeffding count from 1154 to 819 at eps=0.05), not range-1 Hoeffding, so the 'looseness' finding mostly measures a bound nobody would choose; (d) baselines include KernelSHAP-type regression estimators. The variance algebra and the experiment design (exact prediction checked against simulation, fixed seeds) are sound, which a reviewer would credit.

defects.what: No prior work cited: permutation-sampling efficiency (Castro et al. 2009), stratified sampling with Hoeffding sizing (Maleki et al. 2013), optimally allocated stratification (Castro et al. 2017) and antithetic permutations (Illes and Kerenyi 2019; Mitchell et al. 2022) are all published, so findings (i)-(iv) are known results presented as findings; no KernelSHAP or Neyman-allocation baseline.

Stratified vs permutation comparison counts cost in marginal evaluations; in the motivating setting the cost is value-function evaluations (retrainings), where a stratified marginal costs 2 and a permutation yields n marginals for n+1. At equal evaluations the spread-game gain is about 3x (3.1), not 5.9x; README and homepage state '6-8x' and '4x fewer samples' without the qualifier.
The antithetic sampler has no test: replacing idx[::-1] with idx (no antithetic pairing) leaves all 9 tests green; the Hoeffding factor 2 and the strat_var normalisation also survive mutation.

Hoeffding looseness '4-5x' comes from a power-of-two grid; a step-16 grid gives 6.6x and 6.8x. The headline understates looseness, and the comparison uses range-1 Hoeffding when the true marginal range is 0.842 (bound 819 not 1154 at eps=0.05).
E1 header prints 'm=100 marginal evals/player' but m = 100 - 100 % n = 96 for the n=8 games.
Stratum budget is uniform: the k=0 stratum (one empty set, zero variance) gets 1/n of each player's draws; samplers hard-code the toy game's marginal so no user game can be passed in.

verdict: A clean, fully reproducible toy study: every number in the README, whitepaper and homepage recomputes by independent brute force over all 8! permutations (Shapley values, exact permutation and stratified RMSE 0.01831 / 0.00754, ratio 5.89, and the antithetic RMSE the author only simulated, exact 0.01117 vs 0.01118), run.py and the figure reproduce byte for byte, and tests check simulation against the exact variance formulas. It does not meet the bar: verification is 2 (the antithetic sampler is untested and 3 of 5 mutants survive), claims are 2 (the '6-8x' stratification gain counts marginals rather than value-function evaluations and roughly halves to about 3x at equal retraining cost; Hoeffding looseness is 6.6-6.8x, not 4-5x), and fitness is 1: each finding is a known result from Castro 2009, Maleki 2013 and Mitchell et al. 2022, none of which is cited, in one stylised game with n <= 10.
